Upstream pppd 2.5.5 commit 4dc474cacfa045d1ee1b10c388d8c864e3ed3b30.
The auth packet machines and fallback crypto algorithms retain upstream code.
The Windows CLI parses options; upstream option descriptor tables are replaced by empty tables.
Unix system-account/PAM authentication is excluded; explicit secret files are used.
This pppd mppe source derives keys; packet encryption is supplied separately by src/mppe_port.c and the retained Linux MPPE codec in 0.4.0.
TLS/PEAP are compiled only when their static OpenSSL dependencies are available.
CBCP uses the original client protocol: an explicit callback number requests
callback by the remote peer, and its acknowledgement terminates with status 14.
No local modem dialler, call or reconnection is simulated.

Host adaptations and corrections:
- Windows COM/Wintun output and monotonic timers replace Unix runtime calls.
- BCryptGenRandom (Windows) / getrandom (Linux tests) supplies original auth
  challenge generation; no predictable PPP magic-number generator is used.
- Original getword, scan_authfile and string formatter are retained in
  auth_upstream.inc. Explicit secret files are protected by Windows ownership,
  ACL and reparse checks (or strict POSIX file permissions in the native lab).
  Literal IPv4/CIDR, '*' and '-' address rules are supported. Unimplemented
  hostname rules or per-peer options are rejected instead of being ignored.
- The MPPE key functions are compiled as PPP_WITH_MPPE_KEYS for MSCHAP/PEAP
  compound authentication. CCP negotiation and packet encryption are now implemented separately in ccp.c and the data path in 0.4.0.
- The digest registry and MSCHAP response cache reset for each host link init.
- SHA1 explicitly includes stdint.h and uses winsock2.h on Windows.
- MD4's fallback padding copies only complete input bytes, rather than reading
  one byte past a byte-aligned input. ASAN detected this inherited overread on
  the 16-byte password hash. Padding and resulting MD4 digests are unchanged.
  Input bytes are cast to unsigned before 24-bit shifts, removing inherited
  signed-shift undefined behaviour without changing MD4 arithmetic/results.
- LCP RTT formatting preserves upstream %v/%q/%I etc; no Unix mmap is required
  by these authentication sources. The unused %P formatter branch is omitted.
- EAP-TLS client certificate verification uses client=true so that a server
  certificate is checked for serverAuth, rather than clientAuth. Sessions are
  zero-initialized and cleaned up on init errors and link shutdown.
  Local EVP_PKEY/X509 references are released after SSL_CTX retains them;
  chain ownership is transferred without retaining duplicate stack ownership.
  The ticket callback returns zero because it does not retain an external
  SSL_SESSION reference. ASAN/LeakSanitizer checks normal and failed sessions.
- EAP-MSCHAPv2 retains the inner CHAP identifier when sending the authenticator
  response, waits for the client's confirmation before outer EAP Success and
  network activation, and rejects failed mutual authentication even if an
  invalid outer EAP Success subsequently arrives. Retry uses the same message.
- PEAP retains upstream TLS, MSCHAPv2 and compound-MAC algorithms. The existing
  Result-TLV prefix also accepts the complete 11-byte Result-only exchange used
  by FreeRADIUS PEAPv0. It copies the request template into an EAP response,
  requires successful inner mutual authentication, and waits for both a
  successful Result TLV and outer EAP Success before granting the link.
  Result fields are defined by MS-PEAP 2.2.8.1.2:
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-peap/8de89eb4-b4dc-4949-b826-0c30033c4d23
  PEAP initialization is zeroed; separate TLS buffers are freed on shutdown;
  errors from trust configuration, random generation and MAC verification fail
  the authentication. The cryptobinding packet path is retained.
- CBCP validates option bounds/types and ACK identifiers before changing state.
- Authentication cleanup is deferred until a packet callback returns, so that
  an LCP close caused by failed TLS authentication cannot free a live callback.

Inherited PEAP limitations remain: client role, no fast reconnect, no inner
EAP fragmentation, no general retransmission handling. Cryptobinding remains
available, while no IP data encryption is claimed.

Validation: auth_interop.py exchanges real packets between independent protocol
processes, including password failures, TLS 1.2/1.3, invalid CA, wrong name/EKU,
forged MSCHAPv2 authenticator response plus outer Success, and CBCP packets.
Additional lab tests exercise native Linux pppd and an independent FreeRADIUS
PEAP authenticator. Test result artifacts are in the package tests directory.
